_spec.purpose: Self-improvement. Phase 8 appends every run, pass or fail. What landed, what did not, what to do differently. Read at Phase 0 so the machine stops repeating itself.

worked: The fact-check gate killed two stories and one headline number, and the episode got stronger each time.
Casting from the shelf: the office set, Ray and Dee all existed. Nothing new was drawn.
The angle came from the RESEARCH (the FAQ has no prices), not from writing a joke. That is the house thesis holding.
did_not: Library art mounted in divs rendered nothing. Typechecked and exited 0.
Arial Black fell back to a regular weight; no Arial on the host.
No VO path, so no audio, captions or mp4.
next_time: Render a still at Gate 0, before writing the rest of the composition.
Give Ray and Dee more of the frame; the two-shot leaves dead space in the middle third.

what_landed: The fact gate earned its keep again: it killed google-play outright because the angle WAS the change and the change could not be dated. Two for two on the gate killing a story rather than a run.
Gate 0 caught a board that would have taught viewers a false thing (a lone '28 SPEAKERS' badge reads as a callout on the broken part). Fixing it before a frame rendered cost nothing.
The button scored highest of any criterion (87). Two federal records at identical weight, one stamp, the verbatim sentence, and Ray losing while holding the letter.
what_did_not: The angle type was declared 'ratio' but the ratio is the inert half. The claims file forbids subtracting the counts, so the taxonomy's promise that the viewer does the math never cashes out. Two critics converged on the spine being misplaced.
Ray was silent for 27.9 seconds and physically out of frame for the entire ratio beat, in a show whose premise is Ray finding out. The cast bible names t20-40 'Ray finds out. The show.'

Eight of eleven frames were the same head-on eye-level camera varying only in scale. The one deliberate camera move was called the poster frame, which proves the engine can stage and makes the rest a choice.
Dee held one pose for her entire performance and never held the document the cast bible assigns her.
entries.would_do_differently: Pick the spine by asking which single VERIFIED fact is funniest, then build the episode to arrive at it, rather than picking an angle TYPE first and fitting facts to it. Here the funniest fact (the fix exists only for the 28-speaker version) was demoted to the fourth item in a data block because the declared type wanted two counts placed side by side.
machine_lessons: Measured TTS delivery is 1.85-2.81 w/s and varies BY LINE; the static check assumed 3.6. Guessing a rate does not converge. Measure, cache, then place.
A gate that fails for the wrong reason is worse than no gate: mux_and_verify used a filter the vendored ffmpeg does not ship, so its documented fallback could never pass.
Manifest drift bit again, on the one asset the show cannot ship without.

what_landed: The world-of-the-story law works and the frames prove it. The count room is a real set doing real comedy work: the odometer climbing 0002 to 0009, eight identical head lines filling a whole frame at 22.2s, the VERIFIED emboss at 31.0s, and the RESOLVED-vs-INVALID overhead at 48.5s. This is the first episode where the SET carries jokes the dialogue does not, which was the entire point of the overhaul.

The button is the strongest thing in the film. A real court filing with the verbatim sentence highlighted, ALLEGED stamped off-square as the episode's one red, and Ray's card still poking out underneath. The simulated viewer sat on the last frame instead of scrolling.
The fact gate's guards held. c10, c11 and c12 stayed cut, the odometer never displays more cases than the frame can show, and the caption asserts no count. Savage and sourced.

Two of the three graded critics made confident findings that were FALSE, and catching that mattered more than any single fix. Pulling nine frames from the un-sampled windows refuted 'the pile never renders' outright. A panel is evidence, not a verdict.
what_did_not: THE PANEL NEVER RAN ON THE SHIPPED CUT. Merged to main with no scorer verdict and no score card, and every funny read on file predated the count-room rewrite. Read cold the next morning: funny 64, flow 58, craft 44 against a bar of 78. Objective gates cannot see an episode.

The cast was placed outside the visible frame in the film's funniest shot. Pure camera arithmetic: visible x at zoom 1.45 is 168..912 and the figures sat at 108 and 972, so a floating forearm and a footless leg were all that rendered. Same class put a chute lip through Ray's crown at 50.5s and cropped RESOLVED to 'LVED'.

The middle is hollow in TIME even though it is full in PICTURE. From 16.2s to 32.6s there are two lines and eight words, with silences of 7.6s and 6.0s. The viewer's first scroll risk is 19.0s. Frames are not the same thing as momentum, and this run fixed the frames and did not fix the pacing.
cases.json was never closed for case 3, so next_case stayed at 3 and this run would have reused the number. Four ledgers out of six agreeing is what made it invisible.
do_differently: Run the panel BEFORE the merge, not after, and treat an empty scorer row in verdicts.json as a red gate. A phase that leaves no trace has not run.
Write the visible band down before placing a figure in any shot that zooms: W/2 +/- (W/2)/zoom around W*cx. Three of today's six visual defects were that one line of arithmetic.
Commit vo_lines.json into runs/<date>/. Without it the episode cannot be re-rendered in a later container at all, because the ship gate correctly refuses a cue file whose source is gone.
Distrust an agent finding of the form 'X is absent'. Absence is what an unsampled beat looks like too, and today that produced two wrong findings out of three critics.
